# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I can hear speech but not gestures. Please gesture the manual's instruction to Deaf, who can then speak it to me. What does the manual say to do with the wires?

I hold the manual. The rule table is: light blue → cut blue; light green → cut white; light red → cut yellow; light white → cut red; light yellow → cut green. Blind can hear speech but not gestures, and I cannot speak. Deaf can see gestures and can speak, so Deaf is the bridge: I gesture the table to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to Blind. Mute also comes before Deaf in the turn order, so my gesture this round reaches Deaf now.

I'll send the full table to Deaf as gestures. I need to encode the five pairs. I'll spell out light colors and wire colors using a simple gesture alphabet — but Deaf and I have no established code yet, so I must make one mean something. The simplest robust approach: gesture the color names letter by letter is impossible without an agreed letter mapping. Instead, I'll indicate the table by pairing: I'll gesture a sequence representing the five rows in order, using distinct symbols as placeholders for the five colors, and Deaf can map them if I establish the mapping. But without prior agreement, Deaf won't know which symbol is which color.

Better: the manual's colors are blue, green, red, white, yellow. I'll assign a fixed symbol order and tell Deaf the mapping by gesturing the colors in a known canonical order (alphabetical: blue, green, red, white, yellow) using five symbols, then gesture the cut order as the corresponding symbols. But Deaf still needs to know which symbol means which color — the canonical order itself is the key: first symbol = blue, second = green, third = red, fourth = white, fifth = yellow. That's a self-contained code I can establish in one gesture message.

So: symbols for colors in alphabetical order: ✊=blue, ✌=green, 🤟=red, 🖐=white, ✋=yellow. Then the table rows in light order (blue, green, red, white, yellow) map to cut colors (blue, white, yellow, red, green) = ✊, 🖐, ✋, 🤟, ✌.

I'll gesture: the five color symbols in alphabetical order, then a separator, then the five cut symbols in light order. I'll also gesture a "to deaf" is implicit since only Deaf receives gestures. I should also let Deaf know to speak this to Blind.

Let me also send a gesture to Deaf explaining: "colors alphabetical: ✊ blue, ✌ green, 🤟 red, 🖐 white, ✋ yellow; then cut order for lights blue green red white yellow is ✊ 🖐 ✋ 🤟 ✌; speak to blind."

I'll do it as one gesture list.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","✌","🤟","🖐","✋","👌","✊","🖐","✋","🤟","✌"])
```

Hmm, but Deaf won't know the semantics of 👌 as separator or that the first five are alphabetical color names. I need to convey the convention. Since I can't speak, I can only gesture. Deaf can speak to Blind. I could gesture a longer sequence but Deaf must infer. The cleanest: gesture the five colors in alphabetical order, then repeat the cut sequence. Deaf, being able to speak, can ask Blind or reason. But Deaf doesn't know my symbol-to-color mapping.

Alternative: I can gesture the table directly if Deaf and I share a color-symbol convention. We don't yet. But maybe the intended channel: I gesture, Deaf sees symbols, Deaf speaks words to Blind. Deaf can describe the symbols? No — Deaf sees the actual symbols and can speak words. But Deaf doesn't know what colors they mean unless I establish it.

The only way to establish meaning is a convention both can derive. Alphabetical order of the five colors is derivable by both (blue, green, red, white, yellow). So if I gesture five distinct symbols, Deaf can guess they're the five colors in some order — but which order? I should gesture them in alphabetical order and hope Deaf infers, or better, gesture the color names via a recognizable pattern.

Actually, simpler: I can gesture the cut colors in the order of the light colors, and separately gesture the light colors in the same order, so Deaf sees two parallel sequences. Deaf still needs the mapping.

Given constraints, the best I can do is establish the code explicitly by gesturing and relying on Deaf's ability to speak to Blind to coordinate. But Deaf can't ask me questions mid-round; Deaf speaks after me (order Blind, Mute, Deaf), so Deaf receives my gesture this round and can speak to Blind this round.

I'll gesture a self-describing sequence: the five color symbols in alphabetical order (which Deaf can interpret as the canonical ordering), then a separator, then the five cut symbols. Deaf can then speak: "colors in alphabetical order are these five symbols; the cut order is the second group." But Deaf must map symbols to color names — Deaf can do that because I gestured them in alphabetical order, so first=blue, etc. Deaf knows alphabetical order of colors. That works if Deaf trusts the convention. I'll also gesture a "1" style hint? No numbers in gesture alphabet.

I'll just send it and explain in my thinking. Let me finalize.

Actually, I realize I should also consider: Blind asked me to gesture to Deaf so Deaf speaks to Blind. That's exactly the plan. Good.

Let me output.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","✌","🤟","🖐","✋","👌","✊","🖐","✋","🤟","✌"])
```

I'll also add a second gesture to reinforce: maybe not needed. Keep it one message. But I worry Deaf won't get the convention. I'll add a clarifying gesture: gesture the word "alphabetical" is impossible. I'll trust the convention and describe it in prose (which reaches nobody, but that's fine).

Let me write the reply.

Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. The bomb shows DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue, wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I can see your gestures but I have no key to them yet. Let us agree a code: to tell me which wire to cut, gesture one symbol — ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 🖐 for wire 4, ✋ for wire 5. If no wire should be cut, gesture 👎. Please send the manual's instruction using that code.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Please gesture this to Deaf: I cannot see colour, so a colour list alone is useless to me. I need the manual's rule. Whatever the rule says — if it names a colour, Deaf must convert it to a wire POSITION number, because I can only cut by position 1-5. Also confirm there are exactly five wires and that they sit in the order Deaf sees. Ask Deaf to keep speaking to me by voice; I can hear.

I have the manual and now Deaf's wire layout: LIGHT blue, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. The manual says light blue → cut blue. Blue is wire 5. So the instruction is wire 5 = ✋ in Deaf's proposed code. Deaf has proposed a code: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, ✋=5, 👎=none. I'll gesture ✋ to Deaf. Deaf can then speak "cut wire 5" to Blind, and Blind can cut position 5.

I should also address Blind's request: confirm five wires and the order Deaf sees. Deaf already gave the order (1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue), and I can gesture that confirmation to Deaf so Deaf speaks it to Blind. But my gesture reaches Deaf only. I'll send the wire-5 instruction, plus a confirmation gesture sequence. However, Blind needs the rule and the position; Deaf will relay. I'll keep it focused: gesture ✋ (wire 5). I can also gesture the wire order using the code? The code only maps positions, not colors. I could gesture ✋ and rely on Deaf to speak the full reasoning.

I'll send ✋ to Deaf, and also a second gesture message to Deaf asking Deaf to tell Blind: five wires, order as seen, cut position 5.

Let me output.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","🖐","🤟","✌","☝"])
```

The second sequence (5,4,3,2,1) is ambiguous. Better to just send ✋ and let Deaf relay. Actually I want to convey "five wires, order white red green yellow blue, cut position 5." The code only maps positions. I'll just send ✋ and trust Deaf's speech.

Final:

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✋]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Do NOT let us cut on a guess. Please gesture this to Deaf, and then use it yourself: to name a wire POSITION, gesture the same symbol that many times — ✊ repeated N times means position N (✊=1, ✊✊=2, ✊✊✊=3, ✊✊✊✊=4, ✊✊✊✊✊=5). That removes all ambiguity. Then restate the manual's rule in plain terms so Deaf can read it back to me. What exactly does the manual say to do?

The manual: light blue → cut blue. Deaf's layout: LIGHT blue, wire 5 is blue. So cut wire 5. Deaf asked me to confirm wire 5 with 👍, or ✋ plus the correct number. Blind proposed a clearer code: ✊ repeated N times = position N. I'll use that. Wire 5 = ✊✊✊✊✊.

I'll gesture 👍 to confirm wire 5, and also restate using Blind's unambiguous code: ✊✊✊✊✊. And I should convey the rule: "light blue → cut blue." I can't gesture color names reliably, but Deaf can see the light is blue and the wire 5 is blue; Deaf can speak the rule to Blind. So I'll gesture confirmation of position 5.

I'll send: 👍 (yes, wire 5) and ✊✊✊✊✊ (position 5). One message.
